raw.rationale: Temoporfin is a photodynamic therapy agent that requires light activation to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species, so in a standard 5-day dark PRISM viability assay it should show little to no selective killing; any apparent lineage selectivity would be weak and largely nonspecific. Published PRISM-type screens generally find photodynamic agents inactive without illumination, so probabilities are low across all lineages.
